I checked 15 claims and flagged none. All of them are backed by the record.

- **Cause:** The cause sentences rest on Code-Fix's reading (F1) and the logged division-by-zero line (G5309). They're marked as unverified or hedged with "likely", so they don't claim more than the record shows.
- **Timing:** The flag's evaluations went from all off (02:12–02:13) to split (02:14) to all on (02:15–02:20). This lines up with the switch-on at 02:14:28 and with the errors starting at 02:14.
- **Ruled-out flag:** The other flag was switched on at 02:20:18, after the 02:14 onset. By then the error rate had already peaked at 02:15.
- **"Nothing was seen" claims:** The record shows no pre-release check and no staged rollout, so saying none was seen holds.
- **Nobody paged:** The record states this directly. "No person was called" means the same as not paged. It is not the "no one was told" wording the record warns against.

The action items and the what-if clauses weren't judged.

supported.quote: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend figure goes through average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's total by the number of purchases made this month and has no case for a shopper who bought nothing this month. For such a shopper the number is zero, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and the page request fails. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

Turning on a feature switch made shoppers' account pages work out their average spend per item this month, and that sum fails by dividing by zero, likely for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.
If monthly-spend-feature is switched on again before a fix is in place, account pages could fail again, likely for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.
Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Shoppers' account page requests failed with errors, and the account page error rate stayed high minute after minute.
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.

At {P1.1} the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on. Before that, its evaluations came back all off. In the minute it was switched they were split, and after that they were all on. The division-by-zero errors began in the minute the flag was switched.
The switch-on of the flag an-unrelated-feature at {P2.1}. It came after the onset at {T6.2}, by which time the account page errors were already high.
With the flag on, the account page divides the month's spend by the number of purchases made this month, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought nothing this month.
No check was seen before monthly-spend-feature was switched on in production that ran the flag-on code path for a shopper with no purchases this month.
The flag went from off for all evaluations to on for all evaluations straight away.
No staged rollout to a small share of shoppers, and nothing that stops a rollout on rising errors, was seen.
An error while working out the spend summary failed the whole account page request rather than only leaving out that figure.
Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was called to the incident.
